subject: Island 014 Royal Palace monolithic extruded cathedral hull naked macro shell

reviewPolicy.hiddenViews: secondary volume-coherence evidence only; source likeness is not scored where the source provides no exact hidden authority

perViewScores.note: The palace now occupies the court continuously and no pylon gap remains, but the inhabited cathedral is replaced by a huge rectangular lower wall and stacked terrace slabs. The shoulder domes are mostly buried and the source's broad domed-tower silhouette is absent.

The exact front-three-quarter comparison reads as a stepped bunker/ziggurat. Long flat walls, terrace bands, and a thin keep-on-platform hierarchy are materially unlike the compact ornate cathedral mass in the source.
The side exposes a flat single-depth extruded card: a near-rectangular wall with horizontal ledges and hemispheres placed on terraces. It has volume but not credible cathedral depth articulation.
Rear-oblique evidence confirms a monolithic stepped block with diagonal triangulation artifacts rather than nested architectural volumes.
The rear is closed and symmetric, but the dominant blank rectangular hull and shelf-like shoulders are a flat-card solution, not a believable palace back volume.
The opposite rear-oblique view repeats the ziggurat silhouette, blank side plane, and terrace-mounted dome grammar.
The opposite side confirms the flat single-depth extrusion and weak side/rear architectural credibility.
The second front-adjacent view confirms that stepped slabs, not embedded domed cathedral bays, control the silhouette.

representationAssessment.finding: The representation solves continuity literally but not architecturally. Its single extrusion turns the palace into a stack of broad planar slabs, suppresses the domed shoulders, and creates flat-card side views.

vetoes.finding: Large uninterrupted front/side planes and nearly constant extrusion depth dominate; side views read as a rectangular card with ledges rather than a deep cathedral.
The lower hull is organized as stacked horizontal terraces that bury the shoulder domes and produce a stepped bunker silhouette foreign to the source.
The keep remains visually isolated atop the upper slab rather than growing from a dense inhabited cathedral body.

largestMismatch: The source is a compact vertical cathedral composed of interlocked inhabited bays and dominant domed shoulders. This family substitutes a wide blank rectangular hull and stacked terrace shelves, so the palace reads as a ziggurat/bunker with a keep and loose domes on top.
terminalReason: The worst required score is 0.35, far below the 0.75 retirement floor, and the contract's flat-card and thin-keep-on-platform strict rejects are present. Correcting those defects would require replacing the single-depth extruded-hull grammar, not a bounded variable adjustment.
